title: Development of a Real-time Airfare Price Index for India through Automated Web Scraping of Airline and Online Travel Aggregator Portals for Augmentation of the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
description:
• Background The Consumer Price Index (CPI) released by the National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), is the primary measure of retail inflation in India and is used by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for setting monetary policy under the flexible inflation-targeting framework. The current CPI framework, however, collects 'Transport and Communication' sub-group prices, including air travel fares, primarily through manual price-collection from a limited set of outlets and ticketing offices. With over 90% of domestic air tickets in India now sold online through airline websites and Online Travel Aggregators (OTAs) such as MakeMyTrip, Yatra, EaseMyTrip, Cleartrip, Ixigo and Goibibo, manual collection no longer captures the highly dynamic, route-specific, and time-sensitive pricing that Indian consumers actually face. Airfares in India follow dynamic pricing where the same sector can vary by 200-400% within a single day depending on advance-booking window, day-of-week, demand surges, festival seasons and fuel-price-linked surcharges. There is therefore an urgent need for an automated, scalable and high-frequency data-collection system that mirrors what a real Indian traveller pays.
• Detailed Description The problem statement envisages development of an end-to-end software platform that automatically web-scrapes airfare data from major Indian airline websites (IndiGo, Air India, Air India Express, Akasa Air, SpiceJet) and leading OTAs, cleans and normalises the collected price quotes, and computes a Real-time Airfare Price Index (APIx) at daily, weekly and monthly frequencies. The system shall maintain a basket of representative city-pairs (such as DEL-BOM, DEL-BLR, BOM-BLR, DEL-CCU, BLR-HYD, MAA-DEL, etc.) selected on the basis of DGCA passenger-traffic data, and shall capture fares for multiple advance-purchase windows (T+1, T+7, T+15, T+30, T+45 days). Scraping must handle JavaScript-rendered pages, dynamic CAPTCHAs, anti-bot measures, IP rotation, and session management while remaining compliant with the robots.txt and terms of service of source websites, with appropriate rate-limiting and ethical-scraping safeguards. The collected raw quotes shall be passed through a data-cleaning pipeline that removes outliers, handles missing values, accounts for cancellations/sold-out flights, and separates base fare from taxes, user-development fee and convenience charges. The dashboard must visualise price trends, sector-wise heatmaps, lead-time elasticity curves, and provide an API that the NSO and RBI can consume.
• Expected Solution A working software prototype consisting of (a) a robust, ethically-designed multi-source web-scraping engine using Python (Scrapy/Selenium/Playwright) capable of scheduled daily extraction from airline portals; (b) a cleaned and de-duplicated airfare database with metadata such as origin, destination, carrier, advance-purchase window, fare-class, base fare, taxes and total fare; (c) an index-construction module based on PSD given routes and weights; (d) a web-based interactive dashboard showing the daily Airfare Price Index. The solution must include documentation, automated testing, and demonstrate at least 30 days of back-tested results against publicly available DGCA monthly average-fare data.
summary: Innovation (1/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a travel & tourism problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Travel & Tourism. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on api, real-time. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 17/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Real-Time Airfare Price Index via Automated Web Scraping for CPI Augmentation

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that automatically tracks real airfare prices across airline and travel booking websites in real time, so India's official inflation measure reflects what people actually pay, not outdated manual price checks.
overview.why_it_matters: The CPI directly shapes RBI monetary policy. If it's built on stale, manually-collected airfare data while 90%+ of tickets are bought dynamically online, that's a real accuracy gap in a number that matters nationally.
pain_points: Current CPI collection for air travel relies on limited manual price collection from ticketing offices.
Manual collection can't capture dynamic, route-specific, time-sensitive online pricing.
Airfares can vary 200-400% within a single day, manual snapshots miss this entirely.
overview.background: India's CPI uses manual price collection for air travel fares, but with over 90% of tickets sold online with highly dynamic pricing, manual collection no longer reflects what consumers actually pay.
overview.whats_being_asked: An automated, high-frequency web scraping system collecting real airfare data from airline and OTA websites to build a real-time price index for CPI augmentation.
expected_solution: Automated scraping across major airline and OTA websites.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Incremental as scored, though the specific application (feeding a national economic statistic) gives it real institutional significance beyond a typical scraping project.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate. Web scraping itself is well-understood, but building a robust, high-frequency scraper across multiple sites with anti-bot measures, plus a defensible index-construction methodology, is real engineering and statistical work.

competitive_landscape.note: Web scraping projects are common generally, but this specific application (feeding official government statistics) and the multi-site robustness requirement narrow the field.

innovation.note: Web scraping is an established technique, the value is in the specific application to a real national economic statistic.

invention.note: Robust multi-site scraping with anti-bot resilience, plus defensible index methodology, is real engineering and statistical effort.

technical_feasibility.note: Airline/OTA websites are accessible for scraping (with appropriate rate-limiting and terms-of-service consideration), genuinely buildable in 36 hours.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly improves the accuracy of a statistic that shapes national monetary policy, a genuinely significant, if less visually dramatic, impact.

architecture.note: Scraping infrastructure plus index-construction methodology, manageable complexity.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team comfortable with web scraping and basic statistical methodology. Genuinely achievable and demonstrable, with a rare, direct connection to a real, currently-used national statistic.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Extremely well-evidenced problem (specific statistics on online ticket share, price volatility) makes the case for why current methodology is inadequate immediately clear and credible.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building a scraper without a genuinely defensible index-construction methodology (how do you aggregate route-specific, time-varying prices into one meaningful index number) would miss the actual statistical challenge, not just the technical one.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Research basic price-index construction methodology (how CPI sub-indices are typically built, weighting approaches) before building, the scraping is the easier half of this problem, the statistics is the harder, more differentiating half.

idea_0_4: Choose 2-3 major routes and 2-3 airline/OTA sites to scrape as your proof-of-concept scope, not the full national network.
Research basic price-index construction methodology (e.g. how existing sub-indices in CPI are weighted and aggregated) to ground your approach.
Split: one person on the scraping infrastructure, one on the index-construction methodology.
prototype_4_22: Build the scraper for your chosen routes/sites, handling rate-limiting and basic anti-bot considerations responsibly.
Start collecting real price data over your test window to have genuine time-varying data.
Build your index-construction logic, aggregating collected prices into a meaningful index number.
integration_22_30: Connect scraping and index construction into an automated, repeatable pipeline.
Show your index actually responding to real price volatility (e.g. price spikes near a booking deadline or demand surge) in your collected data.
Test data quality handling, missing prices, sold-out routes, scraping failures, your pipeline should handle these gracefully, not silently break.
polish_30_36: Build a clear visualization of your real-time index tracking actual collected price volatility over your test window.
Rehearse explaining your index-construction methodology, why it's a defensible statistical approach, not just an average.
Prepare to discuss how this would integrate with and augment, not replace, existing CPI methodology.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your index built from genuinely real, live-scraped price data (not simulated), tracking real volatility over your test window, that authenticity, real prices, real changes, is what makes this credible as an actual CPI augmentation proposal.

strengths: Extremely well-evidenced problem statement makes the case for the solution immediately clear.
Genuinely achievable with real, live data, unlike many PS in this batch requiring synthetic data.
weaknesses: The statistical index-construction methodology is a real, easy-to-underinvest-in challenge beyond the scraping itself.
Scraping robustness (handling site changes, anti-bot measures) is an ongoing engineering challenge beyond a one-time hackathon build.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Don't neglect the statistics role, the scraping is the more familiar half of this problem, defensible index methodology is the differentiator.
team_fit.approach: Start scraping real data immediately in hour 0-2, you need real time-varying data to build and demonstrate a meaningful index, this can't be left until later.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard web scraping infrastructure and data pipeline code.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing a statistically defensible index-construction methodology (weighting, aggregation, handling missing/volatile data), that requires real statistical understanding, not an arbitrary averaging approach.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded scraper feeding into a naively-averaged 'index' without real statistical grounding wouldn't actually be defensible as CPI augmentation, the methodology matters as much as the data collection.

data_resource_availability.status: Airline and OTA websites are genuinely scrapable (with responsible rate-limiting and awareness of terms of service), real live data is accessible for this PS, unlike most others in this batch.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not needed, real data collection is achievable, though be mindful of scraping etiquette and site terms of service during your test window.

judge_qna.question: How does your index-construction methodology actually work, and why is it statistically defensible?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific weighting/aggregation approach and how it handles route-specific variation and missing data, referencing established index-construction principles rather than an ad hoc average.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would this be reconciled or integrated with the existing CPI transport sub-group methodology?

judge_qna.question: How robust is your scraper to website changes, which happen constantly on real commercial sites?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be honest about this being an ongoing engineering challenge, not a one-time solved problem, describe your approach's resilience (e.g. structured selectors versus brittle exact-path scraping) and what a production system would need for actual maintenance.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your plan when a major site fundamentally changes its structure?
